description: Service boundary definitions for the Faster Payment Initiation journey. Documents which service owns which entity and event, what each service's responsibilities are within this journey, and how services interact. Cross-capability communication is exclusively via async events on SVC-102. The channel (SVC-017) is the only caller of capability APIs synchronously.
architectural_principles: A service owns its entities exclusively — no shared databases between services
Cross-capability communication is exclusively asynchronous events via SVC-102 (event bus)
The channel (SVC-017) orchestrates the user interaction; the event bus orchestrates the cross-capability consequences
Capabilities never call each other's APIs directly — API calls are only channel → capability
Services fail closed on dependency unavailability for compliance-critical checks (sanctions screening)

services.role_in_journey: Primary orchestrator of the payment lifecycle from the channel API perspective. Owns the PaymentIntent aggregate. Validates account state, balance, and limits at initiation. Waits for cross-capability check results via events. Makes the PaymentCleared / PaymentFailed / PaymentFraudBlocked decision. Debits the account ledger on PaymentExecuted.
api_responsibilities: POST /payments — create PaymentIntent after SCA; validate account status, balance, and daily limit
GET /payments/{id} — return current PaymentIntent status for channel polling
POST /payments/{id}/cancel — cancel a pending or scheduled PaymentIntent (only before PaymentCleared)

publishes: EVT-P01 PaymentIntentCreated — triggers concurrent sanctions and fraud checks
EVT-P04 PaymentCleared — signals that all pre-execution checks are clear; consumed by SVC-009
EVT-P06 AccountDebited — confirms account has been debited; consumed by SVC-014 for transaction monitoring
EVT-P07 PaymentFailed — published on insufficient funds, daily limit exceeded, FPS rejection, or sanctions review
EVT-P08 PaymentFraudBlocked — published when fraud score triggers a block
consumes: EVT-P02 SanctionsScreeningCompleted (from SVC-051) — updates PaymentIntent.sanctions_screening_result_id and evaluates outcome
EVT-P03 FraudScoreCompleted (from SVC-013) — updates PaymentIntent.fraud_score and fraud_risk_level
EVT-P05 PaymentExecuted (from SVC-009) — triggers account debit and AccountDebited publication

decision_logic.payment_cleared_condition: EVT-P02.outcome = clear AND EVT-P03.risk_level in (low | medium | high) — i.e. not block
decision_logic.ordering_note: SVC-001 uses a correlation map keyed on payment_intent_id to track receipt of both EVT-P02 and EVT-P03. Both must arrive before a decision is made. Timeout: if either event is not received within 5 seconds of PaymentIntentCreated, SVC-001 applies fail-closed behaviour.

services.role_in_journey: Executes the Faster Payment via Pay.UK/Vocalink FPS infrastructure. Owns the PaymentExecution entity. Also provides the CoP check proxy — the channel calls SVC-009 synchronously for CoP before creating the PaymentIntent. SVC-009 is a new service introduced by JRN-002.
services.cop_proxy_responsibility: SVC-009 exposes a synchronous CoP endpoint (POST /cop/verify) that the channel calls during payment entry. SVC-009 proxies this to the Pay.UK CoP service and returns the result. This is a channel → SVC-009 synchronous call — not cross-capability event coordination.
api_responsibilities: POST /cop/verify — synchronous CoP check proxy for the channel; called before SCA and PaymentIntent creation
Internal event consumer — no publicly documented API for PaymentCleared consumption; SVC-009 is an event-driven consumer

publishes: EVT-P05 PaymentExecuted — published on FPS acceptance with fps_reference, execution_timestamp, settlement_status = accepted
EVT-P07 PaymentFailed — published if FPS submission fails after retry exhaustion
consumes: EVT-P04 PaymentCleared (from SVC-001) — triggers FPS submission. SVC-009 constructs the ISO 20022 pacs.008 message and submits to Vocalink.

fps_submission_detail.scheme_connectivity: Direct FPS participant via Vocalink infrastructure (build/buy decision: Form3 or equivalent managed service provider)
fps_submission_detail.retry_policy: Up to 2 retries with exponential backoff (3 seconds, 6 seconds) before publishing PaymentFailed
fps_submission_detail.cop_service: Pay.UK CoP service (SVC-009 holds the scheme connectivity; channel does not call Pay.UK directly)

services.new_service_rationale: SVC-009 was not required for JRN-001 (account opening). JRN-002 is the first journey requiring FPS scheme execution. A new service is introduced to own the domestic payment execution concern — consistent with the principle that SVC-001 (Retail Banking Core) owns the customer instruction and ledger, while a separate service owns scheme connectivity.

services.role_in_journey: Stateless screening service. Consumes PaymentIntentCreated, runs a real-time OFSI/UN/EU/OFAC sanctions screen against the payee details, and publishes SanctionsScreeningCompleted. Reuses the same service established in JRN-001 — no new entity or schema introduced. JRN-002 adds payment-specific screening fields to the screening request (payee sort code, account number, amount alongside payee name).
services.stateless_note: SVC-051 owns no entities. All screening results are persisted in: (1) the SVC-103 audit log (OFSI obligation), and (2) PaymentIntent.sanctions_screening_result_id (a reference to the SVC-103 audit log entry). SVC-051 itself stores nothing between requests.

publishes: EVT-P02 SanctionsScreeningCompleted — published after screening completes with outcome (clear | hit | error)
consumes: EVT-P01 PaymentIntentCreated (from SVC-001) — triggers the sanctions screening check

screening_inputs_for_fps: customer_id (from PaymentIntent — for payer-side beneficial ownership chain check)
services.jrn001_reuse_note: SVC-051 is fully reused from JRN-001 with no structural changes. The screening engine is the same. JRN-002 adds new screening inputs (payee sort code / account number for account-level sanctions matching) and introduces a new event consumer pattern (EVT-P01 vs the synchronous call pattern used in JRN-001).

services.role_in_journey: Stateless fraud scoring service. Consumes PaymentIntentCreated, runs ML-based fraud scoring against the payment and account history, and publishes FraudScoreCompleted with a risk score and risk level. Does not own any persistent entities for this journey — scores are stored on PaymentIntent by SVC-001.
services.stateless_note: SVC-013 owns no entities in this journey. The fraud_score and fraud_risk_level output is provided via the FraudScoreCompleted event payload and persisted on ENT-008 (PaymentIntent) by SVC-001. SVC-013 maintains its own internal ML model state and feature store, but these are not modelled as journey entities.

publishes: EVT-P03 FraudScoreCompleted — published after fraud scoring with risk_score (0.0–1.0), risk_level (low | medium | high | block), and model_version
consumes: EVT-P01 PaymentIntentCreated (from SVC-001) — triggers fraud scoring

fraud_scoring_features: Payment amount (absolute and relative to account history)
Payee sort code and account number (known-good payee history)
CoP result (no_match payments receive elevated base score)
Customer account age and payment history
Device fingerprint (from channel session metadata in event payload)
Behavioural biometrics score (typing cadence, navigation pattern — from channel session metadata)
Time of day and day of week patterns
Channel (web vs mobile — mobile has lower false positive rate)

synchronous_channel_calls.purpose: CoP check — verify payee name against receiving bank account
Validate FIDO2/WebAuthn SCA assertion with dynamic linking
Create PaymentIntent — single channel API call to initiate the payment lifecycle
Check PaymentIntent status — channel polls every 1 second until status is terminal

async_event_flow.condition: Only published if both EVT-P02 and EVT-P03 return clear/non-block
